observation_summary: The FastDateFormat 'z' pattern (timezone name) always prints the system default timezone instead of the timezone associated with the Calendar instance passed to the format() method.
hypothesis: The TimeZoneNameRule class was incorrectly using a cached TimeZone instance (the one from the FastDateFormat instance) instead of dynamically retrieving the TimeZone from the Calendar object provided during the formatting process.
prediction: The fix will involve removing the cached TimeZone field from TimeZoneNameRule and updating the appendTo method to extract the TimeZone directly from the Calendar object.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows the removal of the 'zone' field from the TimeZoneNameRule class and the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the appendTo method, confirming that the logic for retrieving the timezone was incorrect and needed to be changed to use the Calendar's timezone.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error where the wrong data source (cached instance timezone vs. input calendar timezone) was used for a computation (formatting the timezone name). This is a classic algorithmic/method-level logic error where the procedure for retrieving the timezone display name was incorrectly implemented. It is not a missing check (Checking), not a simple value assignment error (Assignment/Initialization), and not a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'TimeZoneNameRule class stopped respecting the Calendar instance's timezone, and instead now always uses the mTimeZone of the FastDateFormat instance'
The fix diff shows the removal of 'private final TimeZone zone;' from the class fields.
The fix diff shows the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the 'appendTo' method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a field was removed, the core issue is the procedural logic of how the timezone is retrieved during the formatting step, not just an incorrect initial value.
The capability exists, but the implementation of the formatting logic within the existing class was flawed.
